newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open higher, eyes Ok Tedi.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open higher, eyes Ok Tedi.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open higher Thursday as LME three months rallied overnight to a fresh 13-month high after hitting $2,600 per tonne but then eased back slightly.
The market was mulling the knock on effect of BHP Copper's confirmation Thursday that a dry spell at the Ok Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea may cause production shortfalls.
COMEX July copper was called up 1.00 to 1.20 cents from Wednesday's close of 121.80 cents a lb after making its second consecutive new life-of-contract high.
On ACCESS, July last traded at 123.60 cents, up 1.80 cents from Wednesday's close.

COMEX warehouse copper stocks rose 1,179 short tons Wednesday to 44,961 short tons, but LME copper stocks fell a further 200 tonnes to 127,325 tonnes, well down on the February peak of 222,500 tonnes.
